 Opening Remarks & Introductions



             NextEra Energy Duane Arnold                      ENERCON

   Mike Davis                               Rebecca Gardener
   DAEC Restart Licensing Project Manager   Senior Project Manager (SLRA)

                                            SLR Senior Manager

                                            SLR Manager




                                                                            NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 3
 Background

• DAEC commenced commercial operation in 1974.
• One BWR unit with thermal output of 1,912 MWt,
  output of 610 MWe.
• License renewal granted in December 2010, with the
  current operating license expiring in 2034.
• Ceased operations in 2020. Currently, idled and in
  decommissioning status.
• On January 23, 2025, NextEra Energy Duane Arnold,
  LLC announced its intent to evaluate resumption of
  plant operations.
• Presented the DAEC restart overview and regulatory
  path to reauthorization of power operations.
• Submitted its request for exemption from 10 CFR
  50.82(a)(2), officially notifying NRC of NextEra
  Energy’s intention to return the site to power
  operation.
• DAEC is owned and operated by NextEra Energy
  Duane Arnold, LLC.

                                                       NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 4
 SLRA - Safety

Schedule
• Entered PEO February 21, 2014
• Submit SLRA to the NRC by February 19, 2027
• Entering SPEO February 21, 2034
Proprietary Information

• Minimized in the SLRA
• Affects SLRA Section 4 (TLAAs) and Section 3.5.2.2.2 (Irradiation of Concrete)
Initial Assumptions for the SLRA

• CLB is defined as UFSAR (Rev. 26) and TS (Amendment 311, TS Bases Rev. 305) active prior to Decommissioning
  (UFSAR And TS in process of being restored)

   – SLRA to be updated with CLB information per annual updates required by 10 CFR Part 54
• Cutoff date for incorporating comments from SLRI activities into the SLRA – July 6, 2026

   – Technical comments incorporated, as applicable on a case-by-case basis
                                                                                               NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 5
Note: The SLRA Details are subject to change as the SLRA is completed.

 SLRA - Details


DAEC SLRA will be a full-typical application

 • Section 3 AMR Tables will contain all rows, and applicable notes, for each system and associated
  component type

 • Section 4 & Appendix A TLAAs will be updated with evaluations from SIA & TransWare (TW) deliverables

 • Appendix A
  – Will contain all AMPs & Commitment table will contain all commitments including enhancements & exceptions

 • Appendix B will contain all AMPs

 • Appendix C will contain the dispositions for the BWRVIP Action Items

 SLRA - Details


DAEC AMPs with Exceptions (exceptions listed below each)
 – XI.E4 Metal Enclosed Bus (No Enhancements)
   •   Exception to Element 4, Detection of Aging Effects.
   •   NUREG-2191 Section XI.E4 recommends a five-year frequency for visual inspections when no thermographic
       inspections are performed. This DAEC AMP takes an exception to the five-year frequency, and performs the visual
       inspections on a six-year frequency consistent with the CLB.


 – XI.E5 Fuse Holders
   •   Exception to Element 3, Parameters Monitored or Inspected
   •   The DAEC Fuse Holders AMP takes an exception to inspecting for the following aging mechanisms that are listed in
       NUREG-2191, Section XI.E5, Element 3: Vibration.




                                                                                                 NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 12
 SLRA - Details


DAEC AMPs with Exceptions (Cont.)
 – XI.M30 Fuel Oil Chemistry
   Exception to Element 1, Scope of Program
   The AMP Program Description identifies several representative guidelines of the American Society for Testing and
   Materials (ASTM) Standards, such as ASTM D 0975, D 1796, D 2276, D 2709, D 6217, and D 4057, that may be used
   to monitor, maintain, and control fuel oil quality. The DAEC Fuel Oil Chemistry Program does not use this optional
   modified ASTM D 2276, Method A, which requires a 3.0 micrometer filter pore size. Instead, DAEC continues using the
   earlier non-modified version of ASTM D 2276 which requires a smaller more conservative filter pore size of 0.8
   micrometers. The DAEC operating experience and the general industry Operating Experience shows this to be
   acceptable.




                                                                                                NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 13
 SLRA - Details

DAEC AMPs with Exceptions (Cont.)
 – XI.S5 Masonry Walls
    Exception to Element 4, Detection of Aging Effects
    Inspection frequency may exceed 5 years for areas that are normally inaccessible when the plant is online. These
    normally inaccessible areas are inspected at the next scheduled refueling outages following the 5-year interval.
 – XI.S6 Structures Monitoring
    Exception to Element 4, Detection of Aging Effects
    The DAEC Structures Monitoring AMP takes an exception to monitoring all structures on an interval not to
    exceed 5 years. The areas that are normally inaccessible, when the plant is online, are monitored during
    refueling outages, which occur on a 24-month interval. The following areas are inspected during every third
    refueling outage, which results in a 6-year examination interval:
         Drywell interior                        TIP room                       Steam tunnel
         Reactor water clean-up pump room        RHRSW/ESW pits                 Stilling basin
         Circ Water pit                          RWS Intake pits                Air ejector room
         Condenser bay                           Heater bay                     Turbine area
         Turbine building roof                   Cooling towers                 Diesel generator fuel  oil tank
                                                                                                  NextEra Energy Duane Arnold | 14
 SLRA - Details



Shutdown Environments
 •   Conditions during the decommissioning period at DAEC required evaluation to determine if any new aging effects were
     introduced that could cause significant degradation during the subsequent period of extended operation (SPEO).
 •   Browns Ferry & Watts Bar were reviewed for Lessons Learned
 •   A new section, Section 3.0.1 – Summary of the Evaluation of the Decommissioning Period, will be added to the SLRA to
     summarize the results of the report.
 •   All SLRA Systems were evaluated.
 •   While some conditions during the decommissioning period were potentially more aggressive than they would have been
     had the plant remained in operation, no new aging effects requiring management during the SPEO were identified by
     this evaluation.
